current_fund.raw: RMB 30–50 million/year funding goal within 5 years of founding (grant-deployment target, not a closed-end fund)

strategy.thesis: China's first foundation explicitly organized around a '公益创投' (venture-philanthropy) model dedicated to rare-disease drug R&D: it funds the earliest, most VC-averse stages of the pipeline — target/mechanism discovery through preclinical and pivotal clinical trials, the 'valley of death' venture capital avoids — to act as a catalytic lever pulling in government and social capital. Its stated four-pillar strategy (industry promotion, academic research, translational medicine, and impact investing / 影响力投资) explicitly names impact investing alongside grant-making, distinguishing it from a pure-donation charity.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Runs a '科学创新联盟' (Scientific Innovation Union) convening scientists/founders; supports projects from mechanism/target identification through pivotal clinical trials, prioritizing 'neglected' rare diseases and China-specific patient populations.

summary.en: Launched on Rare Disease Day 2022 in Hangzhou, Ruiou (Hope for Rare) Foundation is described in Chinese press as China's first foundation dedicated to advancing rare-disease research via a venture-philanthropy model, deploying philanthropic capital at the earliest R&D stages to unlock follow-on government and private investment.
summary.local: 瑞鸥公益基金会于2022年2月28日国际罕见病日在杭州未来科技城成立，是中国首家以'公益创投'模式推动罕见病科学研究与转化医学为己任的基金会，专注资助基础研究、临床前及关键性临床试验等最早期、最不受传统创投青睐的阶段，以撬动政府与社会资本共同投入罕见病药物研发。

verification_notes: Confirmed via the foundation's own official site plus a secondary industry-media source (MedSci.cn), so scope/existence is solid. However, the foundation's own article explicitly states its current operating model is unconditional grants without expectation of financial return ('无条件捐赠资助项目，不考虑资助项目的回报') even while branding its overall strategy as '公益创投' (venture philanthropy) and listing 影响力投资 (impact investing) as one of four pillars — so it sits close to the pure-donation boundary this slice is meant to exclude; included because it is the clearest, most explicitly self-identified 'venture philanthropy' vehicle for biomedical R&D found in Greater China, and its own stated strategy includes an investment (not just grant) pillar. HQ Hangzhou, Zhejiang (Yuhang District, Future Sci-Tech City), China (not Hong Kong/Macau). Could not verify specific portfolio companies, named individual co-founders, or actual deployed capital-to-date figures — omitted rather than guessed.
